summary: Returns the value as a scalar, or throws.
description: A primitive that carries a single value: string, number, boolean, symbol or bigint. `null` and `undefined` are primitives too, but they carry no value and do not qualify.
`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

params.message: The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted.
params.strict: When `true`, a string counts as empty only if it has no characters at all; by default whitespace is trimmed first.

returns: the same value, typed as a scalar.

throws.IllegalArgumentException: the value is not a scalar.

examples.title: What passes and what does not
examples.body:
```javascript
requireScalar("abc"); // => "abc"
requireScalar(1); // => 1
requireScalar({}); // throws IllegalArgumentException
requireScalar([]); // throws IllegalArgumentException
```
